methodological_rigor.justification: This dual-center retrospective cohort compares LPD alone (n=54) versus LPD plus a modified perioperative HIPEC regimen (n=55) for resectable pancreatic head cancer, with treatment allocation based on patient choice during counseling rather than randomization, creating substantial selection/confounding risk. Inclusion/exclusion criteria are clearly specified (resectable PDAC head, no neoadjuvant therapy, no vascular resection, ability to receive adjuvant chemotherapy), but the non-randomized design and potential unmeasured differences remain a core limitation despite baseline comparability claims. Statistical methods are generally appropriate for the endpoints (Kaplan-Meier with log-rank, multivariable Cox regression with covariate selection and proportional hazards checks, and standardized mean differences to assess balance), though residual confounding cannot be eliminated in this design.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study is an individual retrospective cohort comparison rather than an RCT, supporting an Oxford LoE of 2b. The clinical question is highly relevant (post-resection recurrence and survival in pancreatic head cancer), and the manuscript reports improved median OS (27 vs 23 months, P=0.045) with reduced locoregional recurrence (14.6% vs 31.5%, P=0.035) alongside similar severe complication rates (Clavien-Dindo >=III ~5.5%). However, two in-hospital deaths occurred in the HIPEC group and the findings are explicitly framed as hypothesis-generating pending prospective trials.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE is appropriate and the manuscript explicitly states STROBE-guided conduct, provides detailed eligibility criteria, intervention description (intraoperative hyperthermic perfusion plus intraperitoneal gemcitabine on POD2 and saline perfusion on POD4), endpoints, follow-up imaging schedule, and recurrence definitions. Key retrospective limitations are clearly reported (non-randomization, modest sample size, follow-up differences, radiologic recurrence ascertainment) along with rationale for not using propensity score methods. Data/code sharing is not described in the normalized text beyond standard software reporting (SPSS), so reproducibility posture appears limited.

novelty_literature.justification: The novelty is in evaluating a modified, multi-stage perioperative intraperitoneal regimen combined with fully laparoscopic pancreaticoduodenectomy across two centers, with survival and recurrence outcomes reported. HIPEC concepts are not new, but application in this specific minimally invasive surgical context and with delayed postoperative intraperitoneal gemcitabine is a meaningful extension. The manuscript also proposes candidate selection criteria and a prospective trial direction, reinforcing its translational positioning.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript presents a clear rationale, a well-structured Methods section (design, procedures, endpoints, and statistical plan), and reports results with concrete effect estimates (median OS with 95% CIs, hazard ratio for treatment, and recurrence proportions). Complication reporting is anchored to standard classifications (Clavien-Dindo, POPF grading) and limitations are discussed in a balanced way including the borderline P value for OS. Overall clarity is strong for a retrospective surgical oncology study.

key_strengths: Clinically important question with patient-centered endpoint (overall survival) and mechanistically aligned secondary endpoint (locoregional recurrence) for a locoregional therapy
Detailed intervention and follow-up definitions, with appropriate survival modeling (Kaplan-Meier/log-rank and multivariable Cox with proportional hazards checks)
Signals of benefit (median OS 27 vs 23 months; HR ~0.58) with no observed increase in severe complication rates in this cohort
key_concerns: Non-randomized allocation based on patient choice leaves substantial residual confounding risk despite baseline balance reporting
Borderline statistical significance for OS (P=0.045) in a modest sample raises fragility concerns and heightens need for sensitivity analyses
Safety signal uncertainty: two in-hospital deaths in the HIPEC arm require clearer contextualization and risk-benefit framing
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a well-reported dual-center retrospective cohort with plausible survival and recurrence signals for an intensified perioperative intraperitoneal strategy after LPD, but non-randomized allocation and modest power keep it in the hypothesis-generating category; it is most plausible for Tier 3 pending major revisions and stronger bias-mitigation analyses.
